title: Lesson 22 - Relationship Scenarios: Which Relationships Propagate Access, Cumulative Impact, Record Types
description: Given a scenario, determine which relationships propagate access, assess cumulative sharing impact, and consider record types.

questions.question: Sensitive child records must NOT be visible just because a user can read the parent. Which design avoids propagation?
options: A lookup relationship with the child object's OWD kept Private and no related-record sharing
An Account Team on the parent
questions.explanation: Lookups do not propagate access, and keeping the child OWD Private (with no related-record sharing) prevents parent access from leaking to children. Master-detail and related-record sharing would couple them.

questions.question: Which statement about cumulative sharing is TRUE?
options: Each access layer is mutually exclusive
A user's effective access is the UNION of OWD, hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, and relationship propagation - so map them together
questions.explanation: Effective access is the union of all layers; mapping the combination is essential because multiple layers can jointly expose a record even when each is individually correct.

questions.question: What is the role of record types in record access?
options: They shape page layouts, business process, and picklist values without changing the sharing table
They grant access to related records
questions.explanation: Record types are presentation/process controls; they do not alter record-level sharing, which is governed by OWD, hierarchy, rules, teams, and relationship propagation.
